newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-SHOWMAN NASEEM PREDICTS FIRST-ROUND VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-SHOWMAN NASEEM PREDICTS FIRST-ROUND VICTORY.

text.p: "Prince" Naseem Hamed has predicted his world featherweight title bout on Saturday will be over almost before it begins.

When he first learned that European and Commonwealth champion Billy Hardy would challenge for the unified WBO and IBF championships, Hamed -- not noted for his modesty -- forecast victory within five rounds.
That was back in March, and as the showdown in Manchester has drawn nearer, the 23-year-old Hamed has scaled new heights of self-aggrandisement.
"I will dismantle him in the first round," he told a news conference this week. "I'm fit and I'm ready, there's no way Billy Hardy can beat me."
Last week Hamed gate-crashed Hardy's gym during a training session and watched his opponent at work on the punchbags.
Predictably, Hamed was unimpressed, seeing nothing to suggest Hardy could rob him of his World Boxing Organisation (WBO) and International Boxing Federation (IBF) belts.

"You're all going to be rolling about laughing when you watch it on TV on Saturday night," Hamed said on Thursday, forecasting an absurdly one-sided fight. "I'm in the best shape of my life and I feel absolutely wicked."
Hamed's self-confidence is justified to some extent by his record: 25 fights, 25 victories and 23 knock-outs.
And while the 32-year-old Hardy, with 36 victories from 45 bouts, has a wealth of experience which Hamed cannot match, the champion is expected to claim victory number 26 within the distance.
Saturday's bout, which tops a bill of three world title fights, will be as much about showmanship as boxing.
The self-styled "prince", who has promised to wear his tassled leopard-skinned shorts on Saturday, is a renowned showman who somersaults into the ring before his fights.

In the other two bouts, Robin Reid defends his World Boxing Council super-middleweight title against Commonwealth champion Henry Wharton while American Ronald Wright defends his WBO light-middleweight title against Steve "the Viking" Foster.
Wharton has the best chance of victory of all three challengers.
His record is as good as that of Reid, who has defended just once since taking the world title from Vincenzo Nardiello in Italy last year.
Foster, 36, has hinted Saturday's fight could be his last -- unless he pulls off a major surprise and defeats the Florida-based Wright, beaten just once in his 37 fights to date.
